summary: AMEC Electric is a Metuchen, NJ commercial and industrial electrical contractor founded in March 1999 by Andy Mayernick, now at 48 full-time employees, five field supervisors and 24/7 emergency service from a single Liberty Street shop. It sells design-build electrical work, generators/UPS, lighting, controls, cabling and bucket-truck service to facility and GC clients (server/refrigeration, food processing, auto dealerships) within roughly a 45-minute radius of Metuchen. Customer intake is still phone/email/web-form with human review, and there is no careers page, online booking or customer portal on the site.

facts.fact: Founded March 1999 by Andy Mayernick; grew from $200,000 in first-year sales to more than $10 million in 2025 and 48 full-time employees.
Five field supervisors with more than 120 years of collective experience; home page states 25+ years serving New Jersey and 24/7 breakdown service.
Single location at 125 Liberty Street, Metuchen, NJ 08840; phone (732) 205-1507; NJ Electrical Contractor License #10162.

Service lines: commercial/industrial design and construction, electrical testing and metering, generators and UPS, lighting and exit/emergency lighting, 24/7 breakdown service, sports/site lighting maintenance, telecom cabling, fire alarm, LED retrofit, control wiring, excavation and restoration.

Company-published Blue Book feature (2021) says the firm had 40 employees, 2020 sales over $12 million (its best year), and a general service region within a 45-minute radius of the Metuchen office, with most customers north of it.

Named niche customers/segments per the same feature: server manufacturers, refrigerated warehouses, car dealerships and food-processing plants; project examples include Driscoll Foods (Wayne), Rent the Runway (Secaucus), Iron Peak Sports & Events (Hillsborough).

Leadership named in company material: Andy Mayernick, President/founder; Brian Schnaak, General Manager of Operations; Maryann Budzin, Office Manager; John Hartnett, Senior Estimator; Danny Bayak and Mike Piazza, Field Supervisors.

Office manager built a computerized work ticket and digital time sheets; field crews communicate by iPad, computer or company iPhone; employees rotate on-call duty for 24/7 service and take company vans home to drive straight to jobs.

Intake is phone, email, or a web form asking for name, work email, phone, company, service dropdown and project details, with the site stating AMEC will review the request and follow up on service, scheduling or quote information; emergency line is the same main number.

No online scheduling, booking widget, chat or customer portal is present; the only self-service login is an employees-only page requiring a single shared team password for paystubs, forms and company documents.

Recent project portfolio covers Lincoln of Wayne (Wayne), Holy Cross Church (Rumson), Rent the Runway (Secaucus), Bridgewater Chevrolet (Bridgewater) and Xscapes Theatre (Howell), i.e. work spread across Central and North Jersey.
Company blog/insights page has four posts, the newest dated August 25, 2022, so published content has been largely dormant since then.

operations_signals: Quote/service intake is agent-free but manual: a web form plus phone/email, with AMEC staff reviewing each request and then following up on scheduling or quote information — no instant acknowledgement of scope, no self-scheduling (https://www.amecelectric.com/free-consultation)

24/7 breakdown service runs on rotating on-call duty among field staff, coordinated by supervisors rather than any visible dispatch system (https://www.amecelectric.com/assets/docs/creating-connections.pdf)

Service area is roughly a 45-minute drive from the Metuchen shop, with most work north of Metuchen, so scheduling is travel-time sensitive (https://www.amecelectric.com/assets/docs/creating-connections.pdf)
Office hours are not published anywhere on the site; the only stated availability is '24/7 breakdown service' (https://www.amecelectric.com/contact)

Work ticketing and time sheets are computerized/digital but appear to be office-manager-built internal tools rather than a named field-service platform (https://www.amecelectric.com/assets/docs/creating-connections.pdf)
Employee administration is a single shared-password page for paystubs, forms and documents rather than individual logins (https://www.amecelectric.com/employees)
hiring_signals: No careers or jobs page exists — https://www.amecelectric.com/careers returns HTTP 404 and the sitemap lists no employment page, so hiring appears to run through referrals/word of mouth (https://www.amecelectric.com/sitemap.xml)

Headcount has grown from the founder with a pickup truck (1999) to 40 employees (2021 feature) to 48 full-time staff per the current site, implying repeated field and office hiring (https://www.amecelectric.com/about-us)

Role structure points to coordination-heavy office work: General Manager of Operations, Office Manager, Senior Estimator and five field supervisors supporting 48 staff (https://www.amecelectric.com/assets/docs/creating-connections.pdf)

Job boards could not be checked: Indeed returned HTTP 403 to automated access and search providers were rate-limited during this run, so no live postings were verified (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Amec-Electric)
review_themes: On-site testimonials are uniformly positive and short — staff described as well-rounded and talented, knowledgeable and efficient, trustworthy and reliable — but they are self-published with no volume, dates or star ratings (https://www.amecelectric.com/)

No negative or operational complaint themes could be sourced: Google, Yelp and BBB review pages were blocked or unavailable to automated access, so nothing is asserted about response times, billing or scheduling complaints (https://www.yelp.com/biz/amec-electric-metuchen)
tech_footprint: Static marketing site by The Block (theblock.me) with no booking, chat, portal or e-commerce components; Cloudflare in front (email obfuscation, Turnstile on forms) (https://www.amecelectric.com/contact)
Google Analytics 4 (G-MR5M5HSV42) is installed, so traffic is measured but no lead-scoring or CRM integration is visible (https://www.amecelectric.com/services/generators)

System-info JSON-LD (Electrician/LocalBusiness) with founding date, phone, address and sameAs links to Facebook and the owner's LinkedIn — structured for local search rather than for automated intake (https://www.amecelectric.com/contact)

Presence in The Blue Book Network construction directory is linked from the footer and cited by the owner as a growth source, i.e. a directory lead channel rather than a bid-management portal (https://www.amecelectric.com/assets/docs/creating-connections.pdf)
Employees-only area with a single shared password for paystubs/forms suggests manual HR document handling rather than an HRIS (https://www.amecelectric.com/employees)
Content footprint is thin and stale: four blog posts, newest August 2022, no case-study depth on the five project pages (https://www.amecelectric.com/blog)
growth_signals: $200,000 first-year sales (1999) to more than $10 million in 2025 with 48 full-time employees, described by the company as growth from one owner-operator to a trusted team (https://www.amecelectric.com/about-us)

Company-published 2021 feature reports 2020 as its best year ever at over $12 million in sales with 40 employees — a larger figure than the current-site 2025 claim of '$10 million+', suggesting volume has moved sideways or down since the 2020 peak (https://www.amecelectric.com/assets/docs/creating-connections.pdf)
Portfolio shows expansion into EV charging, solar, fiber optics, utility tracing and sports/arena lighting alongside traditional commercial work (https://www.amecelectric.com/projects)

Owner has stated intended growth in IT/data-center, pharmaceutical and storage/warehousing segments, which are uptime-critical and generate recurring service demand (https://www.amecelectric.com/assets/docs/creating-connections.pdf)
Still a single Metuchen location; no second office, branch or acquisition is mentioned on the site (https://www.amecelectric.com/contact)
decision_maker: Andy (Andrew) Mayernick, President and founder — listed on https://www.amecelectric.com/about-us and in the company-published feature at https://www.amecelectric.com/assets/docs/creating-connections.pdf; operations second is Brian Schnaak, General Manager of Operations (same PDF)

inferences.inference: Dispatch and scheduling coordination is a likely bottleneck and manual.
inferences.reasoning: 48 field staff and five supervisors are coordinated by rotating on-call duty and supervisor planning ('look ahead, solve problems, build a plan before issues reach the job site'), while the only visible technology is a homegrown work ticket and digital time sheets — no field-service management or dispatch tool is named.

inferences.inference: Estimate/quote turnaround depends on a small number of people.
inferences.reasoning: The company highlights hiring its 'first full-time Estimator' in 2018 and now lists one Senior Estimator; every web-form request is human-reviewed before a quote, so intake volume above the estimator's capacity queues up.

inferences.inference: Growth has outpaced the back office rather than the field.
inferences.reasoning: Employee count rose 40 to 48 with only one office manager and one senior estimator cited in company materials, and employee/payroll documents are still served from a shared-password page.

inferences.inference: Emergency intake likely produces after-hours friction.
inferences.reasoning: 24/7 service is delivered by rotating on-call staff behind one published main phone number, with no separate emergency web path, callback automation, or escalation logic visible.

inferences.inference: Hiring is relationship-driven and hard to scale.
inferences.reasoning: There is no careers page (404) and the owner's stated philosophy is promoting long-tenured staff; with 48 employees and 24/7 coverage, recruiting capacity is effectively the owner's and supervisors' personal networks.

inferences.inference: 2025 revenue may be below the 2020 peak.
inferences.reasoning: The 2021 feature cites over $12 million for 2020 as the best year ever, while the current site claims 'more than $10 million in 2025'; the company does not claim a new record, which suggests a flatter or project-mix-shifted top line rather than uninterrupted growth.

data_gaps: No public review data captured: Google, Yelp (403), BBB and BuildZoom (403) were blocked or unreachable, and web_search/source_check providers were rate-limited throughout, so review themes are limited to the company's own testimonials.

No current job postings verified — Indeed returned HTTP 403, the site has no careers page, and LinkedIn's company page returned 403/404; hiring signals are inferred from headcount growth and role structure only.
Business hours, holiday coverage and any published service-level or response-time commitments are not stated on the site.
Internal software stack unknown: whether they run a field-service platform, accounting/ERP or CRM (e.g., ServiceTitan, QuickBooks, Procore) is not disclosed in any accessible source.
Revenue and employee figures come only from the company's own marketing and a 2021 directory feature; no third-party financial, bonding-capacity or license-verification record was retrieved.
Customer names beyond the five public project pages and the 2021 feature (e.g., Driscoll Foods) could not be independently corroborated because external search was unavailable.
